title: NOT INSIDE, BUT AT THE ALTAR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"He is to lay his hand on the goat's head and slaughter it at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering. Then the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar."'" - Lev 4:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the pattern changes. For the priest and for the whole community, blood was carried inside the tent and sprinkled toward the curtain. For the leader, the blood goes on the horns of the outer altar only. It does not go in.

The principle is consistent: the wider the sin's effect on the nation's standing before God, the further in the blood must go.

But do not miss what remains constant. He lays his hand on the head. The animal is without defect. Atonement is made. Forgiveness follows. The mechanism is smaller in scale but identical in kind.

There is a helpful realism here for daily Christian life. Not every sin has the same weight or the same consequences. Scripture never flattens all wrongdoing into one undifferentiated mass — Jesus spoke of the more important matters of the law (Mtt 23:23) and told Pilate that the one who handed Him over was guilty of a greater sin (Jn 19:11).

Yet every sin, great or small, is dealt with the same way: by substitution, by blood, by God's provision. The size of the failure changes the damage. It does not change the remedy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I minimise sins that seem small, or despair over sins that seem large?
2. Am I bringing all of it — great and small — to the same Saviour?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see the true weight of everything I do. Thank You that whatever the size of my failure, Christ is the remedy for all of it. Amen.
